implementerProof.how: Drove the same surface independently at 64c7b235, with main 4e55b2e0 as the negative control, on a Postgres 16.2 and a NATS of the tester's own. Covered: the out-of-order steps, the newly-started-process steps, the lock check, and the review round's failing-observation case. For that case I took every free Postgres connection slot (max_connections 60, superuser_reserved_connections 0, 51 idle psql sessions) on a newly started process, so the horizon pool could not dial. A resuming stream opened in 12 ms and ended after 10.2 s, and the warning 'event horizon observation failed ... too many clients already' was logged. After the slots were freed, a new stream got the next event. On round 4's head b923561b the same steps kept the stream open 25 s with nothing logged. Load: two 1x after-steps at this head committed 3.99 of 3.99 with 100% answered 2xx. Between them, round 4's head committed 3.56 (box busy before: 41%, 10%, 3%), so 1x on this pod varies more run to run than between the two heads.

proof.criterion: A reader resuming from a cursor never misses an event that commits later with a lower id; a test commits two writes out of id order and a resuming reader gets both in a defined order.
proof.surface: GET /api/v1/events (SSE) cold and with Last-Event-ID, on one and two processes; newly started processes with the horizon held or failing; an event log reset
proof.command: adv.py ooo commit|rollback; adv.py concurrent; STREAM_PORT=17778 adv.py concurrent; adv.py reset; adv.py fresh resume|cold; adv.py heartbeat; adv.py shutdown <pid>; adv.py dialfail <log>; adv.py churn 15; adv.py stall; adv.py lastid
proof.observed: Out of order: 123 open, 124 committed. Nothing was sent, then 123 and 124 after the commit, and a resume sent the same; on rollback only 126, 38 ms after. Concurrency: 3 streams and a mid-run resume each got exactly the 92 committed ids in order, on one process and across two. Reset: the open stream was ended and a resume went on with the new log. Newly started process with a foreign id held: a resuming stream opened in 22 ms, sent 2 heartbeats in 35 s, and got the held-back event 233 ms after the commit; SIGTERM exited in 0.05 s. Horizon pool unable to dial: the stream opened, then ended at 10.2 s with the failure logged, and the process recovered once slots were free. Overlapping 2 s holders delayed frames 1.7 to 2.0 s. Bad Last-Event-ID values are refused 400. 0 SSE order violations in both 1x load steps.
